name: Electric Bicycle
description: A two- or three-wheeled ride with at least one wheel 20 inches or larger, fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in one of three classes: Class 1 pedal assist to 20 mph, Class 2 throttle to 20 mph, and Class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: Two or three wheels, at least one 20 inches or more in diameter, fully operable pedals, and an electric motor of less than 750 watts (Tennessee Code Annotated §55-8-301)
Class 1 assists only while the rider pedals and stops assisting at 20 mph (Tennessee Code Annotated §55-8-301)
Class 2 can be propelled by its motor alone and stops assisting at 20 mph (Tennessee Code Annotated §55-8-301)
Class 3 assists only while the rider pedals, stops assisting at 28 mph, and must have a speedometer showing mph (Tennessee Code Annotated §§55-8-301, 55-8-305)
The motor must disengage when the brakes are applied or a switch is released, and it must meet the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512) (Tennessee Code Annotated §55-8-305)

New e-bikes must carry a permanent label stating the class, top assisted speed and motor wattage; modifying one's speed without replacing the label is a misdemeanor (Tennessee Code Annotated §§55-8-303, 55-8-304)

Class 3 riders must be 16 or older on streets and highways since July 1, 2026 (14 or older before then); a younger passenger may ride on one designed for passengers (Tennessee Code Annotated §55-8-307, as amended by Public Chapter 651 (2026))
Class 3 riders and passengers of any age must wear a CPSC or ASTM bicycle helmet (Tennessee Code Annotated §55-8-307)
Riders and passengers under 16 must wear a bicycle helmet on any class, as on any bicycle
Not subject to motor vehicle laws: no driver's license, title, registration or insurance (Tennessee Code Annotated §55-8-302)

Class 1 and Class 2 may ride wherever bicycles may, including bike lanes, shoulders and bicycle paths and trails, but since April 2026 a local government or state agency may regulate or ban them on any of those, including along state highways (Tennessee Code Annotated §55-8-306, as amended by Public Chapter 651 (2026))
Class 3 is kept off bicycle paths and trails unless the path runs within or beside a street or highway, or the local government or state agency allows it (Tennessee Code Annotated §55-8-306)
Kept off sidewalks unless the local government allows bicycles there and the motor is switched off (Tennessee Code Annotated §55-8-306)
